findings.text: _raster_hex_partition_geometry(rg, zg) calls hex_stencil(shape) with shape=(zg.shape[0], rg.shape[0]) -- z-extent first, r-extent second -- which is transposed relative to hex_stencil's own documented (n_x, n_z) contract and relative to how every other caller in this test (and presumably production) builds shape. This is the root cause the node diagnosed for the vacuous boundary-band instrument. The node correctly worked around it in the test by calling hex_stencil(shape) directly instead of going through this helper, but the helper itself still carries the transposition for any other caller, and no follow-on was recorded for it.

justifications.durability: The repinned test closes the exact gap that made the original comparison vacuous: it now asserts np.any(comparison) and np.any(stable_plasma_core) before trusting an empty-set equality, which I verified is a genuine change in the diff (both assertions are new). It also switches the ring source from _raster_hex_partition_geometry(radius, height) to hex_stencil(shape) directly -- the same call the fixture itself uses to build the topology's Null2D, so the boundary-band computation is now provably in the same flat order as DomainMasks.label rather than by inherited convention. Docked from full marks because the expected_axis values are two hardcoded float pairs at atol=1e-12: a legitimate future change to the spline-authored read (e.g. a numerically-equivalent but differently-ordered solve) would require someone to regenerate these pins by hand with no derivation path recorded beyond the commit message, and there is no companion test guarding the _raster_hex_partition_geometry transposition itself, which remains latent in connectivity_boundary.py for any other caller that still uses it.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced both pillars rather than trusting the logs. (1) Ran the committed gate myself in a fresh CPU process at this worktree's HEAD (which has bf8adad merged): 2 passed in 92.59s, matching the manifest's after_suite exactly. (2) Rebuilt the negative control from scratch -- git-archived 7bff1d5d7e8b30b9a1f8a226989b9daec8d762ed into a clean tree, overlaid the repinned test file from bf8adad, and ran it: 2 failed, with ACTUAL values [1.0096852636396698, 0.18645279538409726] (coarse) and [0.9986607891769985, 0.17424244407984985] (fine) -- byte-identical to both the report's table and the recorded negative_control_log. (3) Cross-checked current-invariance-measurement-4.log directly: inside_cells/comparison_band_inside_cells/interior_compared_cells/interior_label_differences/coil_shadow_cells (327/262/65/0/0 coarse, 478/342/136/0/0 fine) match the report's production-invariance table exactly. All commit SHAs in the bisection table and failure_attribution resolve to real commits with the claimed subjects and parent relationships. negative_control_log's first line states the mutation verbatim per the manifest contract.
justifications.fit: Reuses hex_stencil (already imported and used by the fixture) rather than introducing a new ring-construction helper, which is the minimal correct fix once the transposition is diagnosed -- no new abstraction. The err_msg citing 47b9f996 is a reasonable attribution anchor for a regression-style pin and does not read as a banned plan/ticket label. The two added assert np.any(...) guards are proportionate to the defect (vacuous comparison) and do not over-generalize into a broader refactor. One minor concern: the test still leaves _raster_hex_partition_geometry's transposed hex_stencil call unaddressed in production code, which is out of this node's declared scope (test-attribution only) but is exactly the kind of found-but-unfixed defect the global bug-ownership rule would want flagged -- and the node does not surface it under follow_ons, only implicitly in the report prose.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's driving question was whether the two external-coil null-invariance failures are a production regression or a stale pin, and it answers that correctly and completely: git-archive bisection over nine revisions (071dbeb main, verified: 7bff1d5d and 47b9f996 are true parent/child, 7bff1d5d an ancestor of 47b9f996) isolates the first failing landing to 47b9f9965d15807af87b57fbfed9621cedddcdb7 (2026-09-05, predating the 2026-09-15/21 suspect window), and the later containment-anchor/typed-saddle/wall-promotion candidates are correctly exonerated because their own first parents (9af99050, 05aafeae, 0c92afb7) already fail -- I confirmed 05aafeae51f5 is the immediate first parent of d90a522fe8ac by `git log --format=%P`. The diagnosis that the old assertion compared the spline-authored production axis against topology.grid()'s raw local-fit O candidate, and that the boundary-band instrument was vacuous because _raster_hex_partition_geometry(radius, height) calls hex_stencil with shape=(zg.shape[0], rg.shape[0]) -- transposed relative to the fixture's own hex_stencil(shape) call -- is correct: I read both call sites and confirmed the transposition myself. Production code is untouched, which is the right outcome for a stale-pin diagnosis.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat on both commits (654e63e37b test repin, bf8adad966 evidence record) touches exactly tests/test_hex_flood_coil_nulls.py, docs/plans/null-identification-authority.html, and docs/evidence/archive/null-identification-authority-landed.html -- matching changed_paths precisely. The declared orientation_write_paths also listed docs/figures/null-identification-authority and the reports directory as available scope, but the node did not create a figure, correctly noting in the report that the causal sequence and per-revision measurements are naturally tabular rather than spatial. Bisection ran via git-archive scratch trees (not by mutating the assigned worktree or checking out branches), consistent with the global no-stash/no-checkout-for-bisection rule. No plan-label or ticket leakage in the test's err_msg (it cites the commit hash 47b9f996, which is a defensible attribution anchor rather than a plan/sprint label).
